official.deadline_note: Applications close at 5pm FJT (Fiji Time) on Wednesday 21 October 2026. Applications are emailed to the ACIAR Graduate Officer at the host university (USP or FNU), not to ACIAR directly. Applicants are advised of the outcome late November/early December 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake - applications opened Thursday 20 August 2026 and close Wednesday 21 October 2026, for scholarships available from Semester 1 (Graduate Term 1) 2027
official.status_note: ACIAR states: 'Applications for the 2027 PASS program are now open. Scholarships are available from Semester 1, 2027. Applications close 21 October 2026.' USP and FNU both list applications open 20 August 2026 and closing 21 October 2026 at 5pm FJT.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Tuition is paid directly for the relevant program of study' (ACIAR); 'Full Tuition coverage for the relevant program of study' (USP and FNU).
benefits: Full tuition coverage for the relevant program of study, paid directly
Living allowance: FJD 21,450 per annum (Master's, unaccompanied) and FJD 24,000 per annum (PhD, unaccompanied)
Living allowance for accompanied scholars: FJD 32,472 per annum (Master's) and FJD 34,000 per annum (PhD)
Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Books allowance (currently a one-off payment; FNU publishes FJD 750)
Establishment/relocation allowance, currently a one-off payment if applicable (FNU publishes FJD 1,900)

Research grant of up to a maximum of FJD 20,000 (USP) / FJD 17,500 (FNU) for Master's students and FJD 45,000 (USP) / FJD 40,000 (FNU) for PhD students, covering research operating costs, minor equipment and travel expenses essential to undertake research
Funds to present research results at an international conference
Support from the ACIAR PASS Administration team at the host university: professional development, peer-to-peer learning, research collaboration and higher degree research supervision training
Student work placements and career development under the PASS Program (FNU delivers these through its Job Ready program)
eligibility: Be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu (USP also accepts citizens of the 12 USP member countries)
Be 35 years or below when applying for Master's and 45 years or below for PhD; flexibility is considered in exceptional cases
Meet the eligibility criteria for postgraduate study at USP or FNU, confirmed with the ACIAR Graduate Officer before applying
USP Master's by Research: relevant Bachelor's degree with GPA 4.0 or above (200 and 300 level), or a Postgraduate Diploma plus Bachelor's with GPA 3.5 or over for both
USP PhD: a Master's degree by research, or a Bachelor's degree with GPA 4.5 or above (200 and 300 level), or a Master's with 25% or more independent research and a mini-thesis (SRP)

FNU Master's by Research / MSc with thesis: Postgraduate diploma GPA 3.00+, or Bachelor's GPA 3.5, or Honours Bachelor GPA 3.00, or Master by coursework, or recognised professional experience accepted by the Dean of the College

FNU PhD: Master by Research; or Master by coursework with GPA 4.0 minimum plus a completed research method course; or Honours Bachelor's GPA 4.0 minimum (First or upper Second-class Honours); or recognised professional experience
Be able to meet government and university mandated requirements for travel to Fiji for study at FNU or USP Laucala, or Samoa for study at USP Alafua
Women are particularly encouraged to apply - the Program aligns to ACIAR's Gender Equity Policy and Strategy
requirements: Align the research proposal directly with a research topic listed in the PASS Compendium, or propose a unique topic aligned with one of the broader research themes

Prepare the research intent in consultation with the relevant USP/FNU supervisor and ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor; the research intent must be signed by both the supervisor and co-supervisor before submission
Confirm eligibility (GPA and citizenship) with the ACIAR Graduate Officer at the chosen university before applying
Complete the PASS/ACIAR scholarship application form with all required documents attached as one scanned PDF
Submit the research intent as a separate PDF using the prescribed file naming convention
Public sector employees must supply a letter from the relevant Public Service Commission confirming release from duties for the term of the scholarship
Students may not engage in paid employment while enrolled unless with the express permission of the supervisor and head of the relevant school
documents: Research intent document including the detailed research proposal, signed by the USP/FNU supervisor and co-supervisor
Letters of support from proposed supervisors
Evidence of meeting USP or FNU postgraduate entry requirements (including English competency evidence for FNU HDR applicants)
Public Service Commission release letter, for applicants already employed in the public sector
selection_criteria: A Selection Panel at each university reviews applications; applications are assessed based on eligibility and merit
Alignment of the research proposal with the PASS Compendium of potential research topics and themes, some of which are associated with an ACIAR research project
Strength of the research intent and its supporting budget, which governs the research grant allocation
Projects considering gender, social systems, youth engagement, food systems and climate adaptation are also welcome (USP)
coverage: Tuition: paid directly for the relevant program of study (full tuition coverage)
Living allowance: FJD 21,450 p.a. unaccompanied / FJD 32,472 p.a. accompanied (Master's); FJD 24,000 p.a. unaccompanied / FJD 34,000 p.a. accompanied (PhD)
Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Books allowance (currently a one-off payment; FJD 750 at FNU)
Establishment/relocation allowance (currently a one-off payment, if applicable; FJD 1,900 at FNU)

Research grant: up to FJD 20,000 (USP) / FJD 17,500 (FNU) for Master's and FJD 45,000 (USP) / FJD 40,000 (FNU) for PhD - covers research operating costs, minor equipment and travel expenses essential to undertake research
Funds to present research results at an international conference
Student research grant costs shared between ACIAR and USP or FNU
Allowances for students based at USP Samoa are paid in local currency using the USP exchange rates
application_method: Apply through the host university - USP for Master's by Research and PhD in Agriculture, or FNU for MSc in Agriculture or Forestry with a thesis component, Master's by Research or PhD
Download the ACIAR/PASS scholarship application form and Research Intent Template from the host university's PASS page

Email the completed application form with all attachments as a single scanned PDF to the host university's ACIAR Graduate Officer: aciarga@usp.ac.fj (USP, subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships Application 2027') or aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj (FNU, subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027')
Send the signed research intent as a separate PDF using the naming convention PASS2027ResearchIntent-your name-university-program
Note that incomplete applications will not be considered
official.application_route: Email the completed PASS application form (single scanned PDF) plus a separately submitted signed research intent to the ACIAR Graduate Officer at USP or FNU; ACIAR does not receive applications directly.
official.study_mode: Full-time - students enrolled in a full-time capacity are expected to maintain a full-time study load and may not enrol part-time
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu (USP also lists the 12 USP member countries); Papua New Guinea is not currently included
official.international_eligibility: No - scholarships are offered in the Pacific to Pacific Islanders only and are restricted to citizens of the listed Pacific Island countries currently residing in them
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must be in agriculture, forestry or fisheries and must align with a topic in the PASS Compendium of research topics and themes, or a unique proposal aligned with the compendium's broader themes; compendium topics may be associated with an ACIAR research project
official.research_requirement: A research intent including a detailed research proposal, prepared with the USP/FNU supervisor and ACIAR co-supervisor and signed by both, is mandatory; the research grant is allocated on the basis of the detailed research proposal and supporting budget
official.duration: Up to 2 years (24 months) for Master's students and up to 3 years (36 months, or over if applicable) for PhD candidates
official.description: The Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support (PASS) Program provides scholarships and support to postgraduate students in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at The University of the South Pacific (USP) and Fiji National University (FNU). ACIAR, an Australian Government statutory authority, has supported research scholarships at Pacific universities since 2005, strengthening agricultural innovation systems in the Pacific, and the programme is part of the Australian Government's support to Pacific neighbours.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research, an Australian Government statutory authority)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL score is published. FNU states the medium of instruction is the English language, that students must be sufficiently fluent in English to pursue the HDR Programme, and that HDR students will provide evidence from undergraduate qualifications or other English qualifications confirming their English language competency. USP publishes no English requirement for the PASS scholarship.

not_confirmed: ACIAR's own PASS page does not publish stipend figures; the amounts are published by the delivering universities USP and FNU, which are the official host and administering institutions
No English test score (IELTS/TOEFL) is published by ACIAR, USP or FNU
No published statement that international airfare or transport to the host campus in Fiji or Samoa is covered by the scholarship
The accompanied/dependent living allowance rates are described in the FAQ as indicative only and dependent on personal circumstances
Travel and establishment allowance values appear only in the FNU publication (FJD 1,900 establishment, FJD 750 books); USP publishes the same allowances without a dollar figure
verification.notes: Checked the ACIAR PASS page (awarding body), the USP ACIAR and How to Apply pages, the FNU PASS page and the official PASS-CR 2027 selection-process FAQ PDF for amounts, deadline, benefits, eligibility, documents and submission route; all cross-checked between the official pages.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an Australian Government funded scholarship that pays your tuition directly at USP or FNU, gives you a living allowance of FJD 21,450-FJD 34,000 a year depending on degree level and whether you are accompanied, adds medical insurance, one-off book and establishment allowances, and a research grant of up to FJD 20,000-FJD 45,000. The catch is that you must already be a citizen of, and living in, one of seven Pacific Island countries, you must be aged 35 or under for a Master's and 45 or under for a PhD, and your research idea has to match a topic in the 2027 PASS Compendium. Applications close at 5pm Fiji time on 21 October 2026, so the practical deadline for securing supervisor signatures is well before that date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early to mid-career agriculture, forestry or fisheries professionals from Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu who want a research degree at USP or FNU without leaving the region.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the ACIAR Graduate Officer for your chosen university (aciarga@usp.ac.fj for USP, aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj for FNU) to have your GPA and citizenship checked before you invest time in the application
Download the 2027 PASS Compendium of Research Topics from the USP or FNU page and shortlist two or three topics you can genuinely defend

Contact the named supervisor and co-supervisor for your shortlisted topic early - both signatures are required on the research intent, and co-supervisor travel and email turnaround is the usual bottleneck
Draft the research intent using the official Research Intent Template 2027 and build a realistic budget, because the research grant is awarded on the strength of that proposal and budget
Assemble certified transcripts, certificates, letters of support from your proposed supervisors and your birth certificate or passport, then scan everything as one PDF
If you are a public sector employee, request your Public Service Commission release letter now - it is a stated requirement and takes weeks to obtain
Watch the recorded Q&A and research proposal workshop sessions on the USP and FNU pages before finalising your proposal
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications - the FAQ states plainly that incomplete applications will not be considered, so a missing transcript or unsigned form ends the bid
A research intent that is not signed by both the USP/FNU supervisor and the ACIAR co-supervisor
Proposing research that does not map to a compendium topic or broader theme, or a proposal the named supervisor has not agreed to
GPA below the university-specific thresholds (USP requires 4.0 at 200/300 level for direct Master's entry and 4.5 for PhD; FNU routes are lower but still specific)
Submitting after the 5pm FJT cut-off on 21 October 2026 or sending the package to the wrong university contact
Being outside the age caps (35 for Master's, 45 for PhD) without an exceptional-circumstances case already lodged
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare and transport to the USP or FNU campus is not published as covered, and the establishment and book allowances are one-off sums; dependent costs beyond the accompanied living allowance rate, which the FAQ describes as indicative only, plus any personal and visa-related expenses, must be self-funded.
document_audit: The application form and all attachments must be a single scanned PDF, named PASS2027-your name-university-program
The research intent is a separate PDF, named PASS2027ResearchIntent-your name-university-program, signed by supervisor and co-supervisor
Transcripts must be certified copies, not plain printouts
Letters of support from the proposed supervisors and a birth certificate or passport are listed alongside transcripts in the required document order
FNU requires evidence confirming English language competency from your undergraduate or other English qualifications - no test score substitutes for it
The FNU route offers an AI Information Sheet for Applicants that governs how AI may be used and declared in your proposal
alerts: The deadline is 5pm Fiji time on 21 October 2026 - not your local midnight - so applicants outside Fiji should submit days early
Papua New Guinea is not currently included in the PASS program; ACIAR invites PNG researchers to register for updates instead
Paid employment during the scholarship requires express permission from your supervisor and head of school, and public sector applicants need a PSC release letter
Already being enrolled in a Master's or PhD does not disqualify you, but each case is decided individually and needs supervisor and co-supervisor support
Outcomes are only released late November or early December 2026, so plan your 2027 finances without assuming the result
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email one complete scanned PDF (form plus documents) plus a separately named signed research intent PDF to your host university's ACIAR Graduate Officer before 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026, then wait for the late November/early December outcome.
